title: Iterative cycle budgeting and scope decoupling
creator: Avery Chen
description: Introduce an "iterative cycle budgeting" approach to decouple scope from full-team commits. The goal is to create a lightweight, repeatable process that: 1) assigns a provisional effort budget to each initiative at cycle start, 2) enforces micro-slicing checkpoints at predefined cadence points, and 3) defines clear, triggerable scope-cut rules tied to measurable capacity signals (e.g., burn rate, cross-functional pull requests, blocker-days). This ticket covers the product playbook, decision rules, and a small pilot with two initiatives to validate the process and surface tooling gaps in the Cycle Planner and roadmap board.
acceptance_criteria: A concise playbook (<=2 pages) published to Confluence describing iterative budgeting, micro-slices, and scope-cut triggers
Two pilot initiatives are enrolled and have baseline budgets and at least two micro-slices defined in the Cycle Planner
A dashboard widget in the roadmap board shows real-time budget burn and flags when an initiative hits scope-cut trigger (threshold configurable)
A retrospective from the pilots captures at least 3 actionable improvements to the budgeting rules or tooling
Stakeholder alignment: Eng, Design, and Support leads sign off on the pilot playbook and trigger thresholds
